title: A request-scoped async DB connection with commit and rollback
problem: notes.py is a small notes API on SQLite through aiosqlite. Its get_conn dependency opens a connection per request but never commits, never rolls back and never closes it, so nothing is saved and connections leak. Finish get_conn so each request is one unit of work, and implement GET /notes/{note_id}.
requirements: get_conn opens one aiosqlite connection per request from DB_PATH (read at call time)
If the endpoint finishes without an exception, the transaction is committed
If the endpoint raises, the transaction is rolled back and the exception propagates
GET /notes/{note_id} returns {"id", "title", "body"} or 404 with detail "note not found"
contract:
async def get_conn()  # async generator dependency yielding an aiosqlite.Connection
GET /notes/{note_id} -> 200 {id, title, body} | 404 {"detail": "note not found"}
expectedBehavior: POST /notes then GET /notes/{id} returns the note, and a separate connection sees the row. POST /notes/batch with a blank title returns 422 and saves none of the batch. Every connection opened during the requests is closed.
edgeCases: A batch that fails halfway: nothing from it is saved, earlier notes stay
Error responses (404, 422) still close the connection
Call aiosqlite.connect through the module (the tests count connections that way)
hints: Conceptual: a dependency with yield runs the code after yield when the request is done. An exception raised in the endpoint is thrown into the generator at the yield, so try/except/finally around the yield sees it.

Specific: wrap the yield in try: commit right after the yield, roll back and re-raise in `except Exception:`, close in finally. In get_note, use fetchone() and raise HTTPException(404) when it returns None.

Implementation: `try: yield conn; await conn.commit()` / `except Exception: await conn.rollback(); raise` / `finally: await conn.close()`. Query with `await conn.execute("SELECT id, title, body FROM notes WHERE id = ?", (note_id,))`.
evaluation: Commit only on the success path; rollback re-raises
Connection closed in finally (or by async with)
